title: ‘Perfect’ - A Christmas Carol at The Old Vic - review & photos
transcript: a Christmas carol of the Old Vic written by Jack Thorne directed by Matthew arcus and starring Stephen Tomkinson a Christmas carol these days is one of the most popular stage entertainments but there's none better than the one at the old beach and how do I know this because it's perfect we should expect nothing better than the magical production from Jack Thorne and Matthew walkers Jack Thorne wrote Harry Potter and the cursed child and Matthew arc is among many other things directed Matilda here's my review from the moment you arrive you're immediately immersed in the most wonderful magical occasion the cast are already wandering around the auditorium chatting handing out clementines and mince pies up above you there are countless lanterns in the ceiling and the stage itself is in the center of the auditorium with seating all around they know what they're doing in creating an experience which frankly you could only have in the theater where things are happening left right and center up above you get singer suddenly appear in the upper circle what a great idea to have running through the whole performance Christmas carols usually played with them bell ringing as well as singing because Christmas carols are about redemption and hope and that's what this story is about and it's certainly what this production is about because the way Jack Thorne has written this and the way Steven Tompkins and performs Scrooge we see him as a man who has lost his way really he's not a bad man he's taken wrong turns but he is capable of change and capable of helping to solve the problem of poverty the ghosts all played by women are amazingly spooky and and funny and when finally he does see the light Scrooge becomes the center of the most glorious celebration and the brilliant steam Tomkinson lead spell ringing dancing food pouring onto the stage and there's even snow I didn't want it to and I give a Christmas carol at the Old Vic starring Stephen Tomkinson five stars why not subscribe to future reviews by clicking on the icon below [Music] you
